title: SwiftUI selection binding cannot express a range or single selection set from code
description:
KDCalendarView.updateUIView (CalendarView+SwiftUI.swift:179-187) syncs the binding by calling view.selectDate for each wanted day. selectDate follows tap rules, so in .range mode the days pair up into anchor/complete/new-anchor, and in .single mode each one replaces the last. The delegate callbacks are suppressed while isUpdating, so the binding is never corrected.

Scenario (reproduces in the demo): SwiftUIDemoView starts in .range mode; tap 'Select this week'. The binding holds 7 days and the list below shows 7, but the calendar ends with only the 7th day selected (1-2 range, cleared by 3, 3-4, cleared by 5, 5-6, cleared by 7). In .single mode a binding with several dates shows only the last one.

Fix: apply the binding directly instead of replaying taps, e.g. an internal setSelection(_ dates:) that bypasses mode rules (or uses selectRange for .range from min to max), then write the effective selection back to the binding if it differs.
notes: Fixed in 9e29562. updateUIView now calls a new internal CalendarView.setSelection(_:) that replaces the selection in the mode's shape without notifying the delegate (.multiple: every selectable day in order; .single: the last; .range: every selectable day from min to max, clamped to dateRange; a lone day is the anchor of an incomplete range). If the view then shows something else, Coordinator.correctSelection writes that back to the binding in a main-actor Task after the update, skipped if the binding changed in the meantime. Regression tests: PlatformTests.swiftUIRangeSetFromTheBindingSelectsEveryDayInIt / swiftUIBindingIsCorrectedToWhatTheViewShows (both fail on the old sync) and CalendarViewTests.setSelection*. For bl0.5: in SwiftUI, a mode change now reshapes the binding into the new mode and writes it back (multiple->single keeps the last day, so the demo list is corrected; multiple->range spans min...max rather than clearing as UIKit does). For rlq.1: setSelection is a third copy of the day-fill loop (with selectRange and completeRange). Check: swift-format lint, 95/95 package tests, docbuild (both schemes), demo build all pass.
close_reason: Binding applied as a whole via setSelection(_:) and corrected when the view differs; full check passes (9e29562).

title: Selection is stored as IndexPaths that go stale when the month grid is rebuilt
description:
CalendarView keeps selectedIndexPaths alongside selectedDates (CalendarView.swift:140). refreshMonths() (CalendarView+DataSource.swift:123) rebuilds the grid whenever the data source range moves to other days or the calendar changes, and updateStyle() invalidates it on every style change, but the stored index paths are never remapped. reloadData() (CalendarView.swift:480) then re-selects the old index paths.

Scenario: select 15 March with a range starting in March, then make startDate() return a day in February and call reloadData(). Sections shift by one, so the highlighted cell is 15 April while selectedDates still says 15 March. deselectDate(15 March) then does nothing (the new index path is not in selectedIndexPaths), and tapping the highlighted April cell removes 15 March from selectedDates. A change of style.firstWeekday shifts items within the section the same way. If the grid shrinks, a stale index path can point past the last section.

Triggers in practice: the SwiftUI wrapper changing its range (CalendarView+SwiftUI.swift:166), a data source whose range is relative to Date() crossing midnight (the NSCalendarDayChanged observer reloads), any style change that alters the first weekday.

Fix: make selectedDates the source of truth and derive index paths from the current grid on reload (drop selections that left the range, and tell the delegate). See the structure bead about selection state.
close_reason: Fixed in 564cb5f. selectedDates is the only record of the selection; the range anchor is a Date and selectedIndexPaths is derived from the current grid. reloadData re-selects each day's cell where it now is, deselects days that left the range and reports them with didDeselectDate (this also fixes a crash: re-selecting a stale path in a section the grid lost threw NSInternalInconsistencyException). A time zone change via style moves selected days to the same calendar days. 7 regression tests (range gains a month, tap after the shift, first weekday change, shrinking range, range anchor, time zone, SwiftUI range change); all fail on the old code. Checks: swift-format lint --strict, 97/97 tests on iPhone 17 Pro iOS 26.5, docbuild for both schemes, example app build. For rlq.1: the dates-only storage is done; what remains there is pulling the logic into a SelectionState value type. Follow-ups: CalendarView-do9 (SwiftUI binding), CalendarView-p0p (DST last day).

title: Split CalendarView.swift and CalendarView+Delegate.swift by feature
description:
## Now
CalendarView.swift is 612 lines holding CalendarEvent, both public protocols with their default implementations, the view's stored state, setup, layout, right-to-left handling, time zone moves, the public selection API and the scrolling API. CalendarView+Delegate.swift mixes selection callbacks with scrolling callbacks and the header title. MonthGrid and the Calendar.fixed extension live in CalendarView+DataSource.swift. Finding, say, everything about scrolling means reading four files.

## Proposal
One file per concept: CalendarEvent.swift, CalendarViewDataSource.swift and CalendarViewDelegate.swift (protocols plus defaults), MonthGrid.swift, Calendar+Fixed.swift, CalendarView.swift (state, setup, layout), CalendarView+Selection.swift (public selection API, UICollectionView selection callbacks, the shared apply-change method), CalendarView+Scrolling.swift (setDisplayDate, next/previous month, scroll callbacks, notifying the month), CalendarView+DataSource.swift (cells only). A pure move: no code changes in the same commit, so the diff is reviewable. Best done before or after the other refactors, not in the middle of them.
close_reason: Pure move into one file per concept; lint, 140 tests, both docbuilds and the example build pass. Dependent tickets reviewed and annotated with the new code locations.

title: Let CalendarFlowLayout own the page geometry
description:
## Now
Page arithmetic lives in three files. CalendarView.scrollViewOffset(for:) (CalendarView.swift:461-475) and dateFromScrollViewPosition() (CalendarView+Delegate.swift:128-148) each switch on direction with an @unknown default, pick x/width or y/height and call flowLayout.mirroredPage. CalendarFlowLayout (CalendarFlowLayout.swift:66-129) repeats the same axis choice with isVertical ternaries in collectionViewContentSize, layoutAttributesForElements and attributes(for:). cellSize(in:) (CalendarView.swift:400-405) computes the item size outside the layout and ignores its argument.

## Proposal
Give the layout the whole geometry: contentOffset(forSection:), section(atContentOffset:) and the item size from its own bounds in prepare(). A tiny private Axis helper (length(of: CGSize), position(of: CGPoint), point(along:)) replaces the repeated switches and ternaries. CalendarView asks the layout instead of doing the maths, and mirroredPage becomes private.

## Pattern
Information expert: the object that lays out the pages is the one that knows where a page is.
notes: After the CalendarView-4qn.4 file split (pure move) the cited code now lives at: scrollViewOffset(for:) CalendarView+Scrolling.swift:66-80, dateFromScrollViewPosition() CalendarView+Scrolling.swift:131-151, cellSize(in:) CalendarView.swift:268-273.

title: Apply a selection change and notify the delegate in one method
description:
## Now
Every selection entry point repeats the same steps by hand: work out a SelectionState.Change, show it in the collection view, then report the dropped days and sometimes the new day or range. See selectionMode's setter (CalendarView.swift:194-203), reloadData (485-497), selectRange (555-559), clearAllSelectedDates (562-564), setSelection (568-575), didSelect (CalendarView+Delegate.swift:41-57) and didDeselect (61-68). The comment 'the delegate may read the selection while it is asked which days are selectable, so the change is worked out on a copy' and the copy-then-commit code appear twice (Delegate.swift:43-47, CalendarView.swift:569-573). Whether a path notifies is implicit: clearAllSelectedDates and setSelection stay silent, the others report.

## Proposal
One method, e.g. updateSelection(notify: Bool, _ body: (inout SelectionState) -> SelectionState.Change?), that runs body on a copy, commits it, shows the change and, when asked, reports didDeselectDate for each dropped day and didSelectRange for a completed range. Each entry point becomes one call that states whether it notifies.

## Pattern
Command / transaction: a change is computed, committed and published in one step, so no path can forget one of them.
notes: After the CalendarView-4qn.4 file split (pure move) the cited code now lives at: selectionMode setter CalendarView+Selection.swift:20-29, reloadData CalendarView.swift:312-324, selectRange CalendarView+Selection.swift:68-72, clearAllSelectedDates :75-77, setSelection :81-88 (copy-then-commit :82-86), didSelect :148-164 (copy-then-commit :150-154), didDeselect :168-175. CalendarView+Delegate.swift no longer exists; show(_:) is at CalendarView+Selection.swift:109.

title: Build the grid, today and the event index as one immutable snapshot
description:
## Now
The derived state of the view is spread over five stored properties that are rebuilt by hand in different places: months, todayIndexPath, eventsByIndexPath, formatters (CalendarView.swift:151-155, 237) and the selection's calendar. refreshMonths() (CalendarView+DataSource.swift:149-178) does six jobs: asks the data source, rebuilds the formatters, checks a cache, moves the selection to a new time zone, logs, refreshes today and rebuilds the event index. currentMonths (line 181) is a computed property with side effects: reading it can call the data source and move the selection. numberOfSections(in:) also calls refreshMonths(). The events didSet calls rebuildEventIndex() and then reloadData(), which may rebuild it again.

## Proposal
A value type, e.g. CalendarSnapshot, made by one pure function from its inputs (data source range, resolved calendar, first weekday, events, now): it holds the MonthGrid, the index path of today, the event index and the calendar it was built with. The view keeps one snapshot, rebuilds it in reloadData() when an input changed, and every reader uses it. No computed property touches the data source.

## Pattern
Snapshot / view model: derive all display state from inputs in one place, so the view's job is only to apply it. Makes the grid testable without UIKit and removes the ordering bugs that come from rebuilding pieces separately.
notes:
After the CalendarView-4qn.4 file split (pure move) the cited code now lives at: months/todayIndexPath/eventsByIndexPath CalendarView.swift:73-77, formatters CalendarView.swift:120; refreshMonths() CalendarView.swift:331-360 and currentMonths CalendarView.swift:363 (the grid extension at the end of CalendarView.swift); numberOfSections(in:) stays in CalendarView+DataSource.swift.
Reviewed after CalendarView-4qn.6 (b998480): eventsByIndexPath is now 'var eventIndex: EventIndex' (CalendarView.swift:78), built by the pure EventIndex(events:grid:) in Sources/KDCalendar/EventIndex.swift; rebuildEventIndex() is a one-liner in the grid extension. The snapshot can hold an EventIndex directly; readers use eventIndex[indexPath] / eventIndex.count(at:). Proposal unaffected.

title: Review: simplify and make the code easier to read
description: Refactors from the October 2026 read-through of main at 6db3184 (release 2.1.0). Each child names the current code, the proposed shape and, where one fits, the design pattern. None should change behaviour; the 140 tests are the safety net, and each child adds tests for any new type it introduces. Children labelled api-3.0 change public API and belong with CalendarView-rlq.5.

title: SwiftUI binding keeps days a range change deselected
description:
Since CalendarView-bl0.1, reloadData() deselects selected days that left the data source's range and reports each with didDeselectDate. In KDCalendarView.updateUIView (CalendarView+SwiftUI.swift) the range change calls view.reloadData() while coordinator.isUpdating is true, so the coordinator ignores those callbacks and the binding keeps the dropped days. The sync that follows then calls selectDate for them, which does nothing because they are out of range, so the binding and the view disagree until the next tap.

Scenario: select 20 April, then shrink the range so that it ends in March. The view shows no selection; the binding still holds 20 April.

CalendarView-bl0.2 plans to write the effective selection back to the binding after syncing; if that write-back runs after the range reload it covers this, and this bead can close as a duplicate. Otherwise write view.selectedDates back to the binding (outside the view update) when a reload in updateUIView changed it.
close_reason: Already fixed by CalendarView-bl0.2: updateUIView's setSelection + Coordinator.correctSelection runs after the range reload and writes the view's selection back to the binding. Added regression test PlatformTests.swiftUIRangeChangeDropsTheLeftDaysFromTheBinding (multiple and range mode); it fails with the write-back disabled. Check: swift-format lint, 110/110 package tests, docbuild (both schemes), demo build all pass (cec4875).

title: Keep selection as dates only and derive index paths
description:
Selection lives in four places that must be kept in step by hand: selectedIndexPaths, selectedDates, rangeAnchor and rangeIsComplete (CalendarView.swift:140-216), updated from didSelect, didDeselect, completeRange, deselectAll, clearAllSelectedDates, selectRange and the selectionMode observer. The duplication is what makes the stale index path bug possible.

Proposal: a small SelectionState value type holding the selected days (as start-of-day Dates, ordered) and the range anchor as a Date, with pure methods for tap, deselect, range completion and mode change that return the days added and removed. CalendarView applies the diff to the collection view and the delegate. The type is testable without UIKit. Fixes the stale index path bug and simplifies the SwiftUI sync.
close_reason: SelectionState value type holds mode, days and pending range start; CalendarView applies its diffs. Lint, package tests, example build and docbuild pass. Commit 1d97951.

title: Animated setDisplayDate before layout never reports didScrollToMonth
description:
setDisplayDate(_:animated: true) (CalendarView.swift:493) sets animationTargetMonth and relies on scrollViewDidEndScrollingAnimation to notify the delegate. When the content offset does not change, e.g. the view has no size yet (offset 0 to 0) or the month is already on screen, UIKit sends no callback. displayDate is already set by displayDateOnHeader, so the first-layout branch in layoutSubviews (displayDate == nil) does not fire either, and animationTargetMonth stays set.

Where it bites: KDCalendarView.displayDate(_:) calls setDisplayDate with animated = (transaction has an animation) during updateUIView, before the view is laid out, so onScrollToMonth may never fire for the initial month in an animated update. The README tells UIKit users to call it from viewDidAppear, which avoids it there.

Confirm: a test that calls setDisplayDate(animated: true) on an unlaid-out view and checks the delegate after layout. Fix: fall back to the non-animated path when the target offset equals the current one or the view has no size.
close_reason: setDisplayDate(animated: true) now takes the non-animated path when the collection view has no size or the target offset equals the current one, so the delegate is notified at once and animationTargetMonth is not left set. Two ScrollingTests cover it (red before, green after). Full check passed: package tests (108), swift-format lint --strict, docbuild for both schemes, example app build. Commit 4f7efc6. Follow-up filed: CalendarView-7gw.

title: firstWeekday .automatic ignores style.locale when style.calendar has no locale
description:
Style.effectiveFirstWeekday (CalendarView+Style.swift:177-184) returns style.calendar.firstWeekday for .automatic. A calendar made with Calendar(identifier:) has an empty locale and firstWeekday 1 (verified: Calendar(identifier: .gregorian) gives locale '' and firstWeekday 1; the same calendar with de_DE gives 2). CalendarView.calendar (CalendarView.swift:123) already fills in style.locale for this case so weekends follow the locale, but the grid (refreshMonths) and the header (CalendarHeaderView.updateStyle) use style.effectiveFirstWeekday.

Scenario: style.calendar = Calendar(identifier: .gregorian), style.locale = de_DE, style.firstWeekday = .automatic. Weeks start on Sunday although German weeks start on Monday. The README's Persian example (calendar = Calendar(identifier: .persian), firstWeekday = .automatic, no locale) is affected the same way.

Fix: resolve .automatic against the locale-filled calendar (move the fill-in logic from CalendarView.calendar into Style so both agree). The existing test (CalendarViewTests.swift:128) sets firstWeekday explicitly on the calendar, so it does not cover this.
notes: Correction to close reason: the package test run had 107 tests (the new test included), all passed.
close_reason: Style.resolvedCalendar fills in style.locale; .automatic resolves against it. Test added. Full check passed: swift-format lint, package tests (108), docbuild for both schemes, example build.

title: Changing selectionMode drops selected days without telling the delegate
description:
selectionMode's didSet (CalendarView.swift:185-204) trims to the last day when switching to .single and calls clearAllSelectedDates() when switching to .range. Neither path calls didDeselectDate, unlike every other deselection that changes the user's selection.

Consequences: a delegate that mirrors the selection goes out of sync. In SwiftUI the binding keeps the dropped days, so the next updateUIView re-selects them through tap rules (see the SwiftUI binding bug). The demo's mode picker shows it: select three days in Multiple, switch to Single, and the list still shows three.

Fix: notify didDeselectDate for each dropped day (or document the silence and have the SwiftUI coordinator write back view.selectedDates after the mode changes).
close_reason: Mode change now sends didDeselectDate per dropped day; KDCalendarView writes the trimmed selection back to its binding. Commit cb27e5b. Lint, 108 tests, docbuild and demo build pass.

title: loadEvents() silently misses events when the range spans more than four years
description:
EKEventStore.predicateForEvents(withStart:end:calendars:) only matches events within a four-year span; a longer interval is shortened to its first four years (documented EventKit behaviour). EKEventStore.events(from:to:) (EventsManager.swift:60) passes the data source's whole range, and CalendarView.loadEvents() (EventsManager.swift:126) uses dateRange as is.

Scenario: a data source from 2020 to 2030. Events after 2024 never appear and no error is reported.

Fix: split the interval into chunks of at most four years (less a day) in the EKEventStore conformance and concatenate the results, de-duplicating by eventIdentifier if needed. Test with the fake store that load() still receives the full range, and with a chunking helper that is unit-testable.
close_reason: EKEventStore.events(from:to:) now queries in chunks of 4 years less a day and de-duplicates by (eventIdentifier, startDate). Helper EventsManager.queryIntervals is unit-tested; loadEvents test confirms the store still receives the full range. Package tests (105) pass, swift-format lint passes, KDCalendarEventKit docbuild succeeds. Commit c992354.

title: Reused cells keep the previous day's VoiceOver label on adjacent days
description:
collectionView(_:cellForItemAt:) sets accessibilityLabel only for days of the month (CalendarView+DataSource.swift:249-252). CalendarDayCell.clearStyles() (CalendarDayCell.swift:83) resets the flags, date and text but not accessibilityLabel, and every cell stays an accessibility element.

Scenario: with style.showAdjacentDays = true, scroll between months so a cell that showed 'Monday, 5 February 2024' is reused for a trailing adjacent day showing '2'. VoiceOver reads 'Monday, 5 February 2024' for it.

Fix: reset accessibilityLabel in clearStyles(), and either give adjacent days their own label or set isAccessibilityElement = false for them (they are not selectable). Add a test that reuses a cell as an adjacent day.
close_reason: Fixed in 95948cc: clearStyles() resets accessibilityLabel; adjacent days are not accessibility elements. New test reusedCellsDoNotKeepTheirVoiceOverLabelAsAdjacentDays fails on the old code. Lint, 103 package tests, both docbuilds and the example build pass.

title: Name and group Style's properties by what they colour
description:
## Now
Style has about 30 flat properties whose names do not say what they colour: cellColorOutOfRange and cellColorAdjacent are text colours, cellColorDefault and cellSelectedColor are backgrounds, cellTextColorDefault is text, and the prefixes switch between cellColorX, cellXColor and cellTextColorX (CalendarView+Style.swift). Finding the right property means reading each doc comment.

## Proposal
Group into nested values with consistent names, e.g. style.day.text / .background / .border for each state (default, today, selected, weekend, outOfRange, adjacent), style.header, style.weekdays. Keep the flat names as deprecated computed properties forwarding to the new ones for one release. Decide together with CalendarView-rlq.5.
notes: Deferred with CalendarView-rlq.5: a public API change for 3.0 that needs the maintainer's decision, not an unattended worker. Undefer to schedule it.

title: Share the test fixtures instead of copying them into every suite
description:
## Now
The seven test suites each define their own helpers: a host window (5 copies), date(_:_:_:) (7), makeCalendar(...) (6, with slightly different parameters), cell(_:_:) (5) and delegate(of:) (3); e.g. CalendarViewTests.swift:56-105, ScrollingTests.swift:53-99, IssueTests.swift:45-99, EngineTests.swift:29-73, PlatformTests.swift:29-66. A change to how a calendar is set up for tests (as the data-source-reload fix needed) has to be repeated in each.

## Proposal
A TestSupport.swift with a CalendarFixture (window, UTC calendar, date helper, makeCalendar with defaulted parameters for range, frame, calendar, locale and first weekday, cell lookup, recording delegate and fixed data source). Suites keep only what is specific to them. A pure test refactor; the test count must stay the same.
close_reason: TestSupport.swift adds UTCDates and CalendarFixture (a window per suite, makeStyle/makeCalendar with defaulted parameters, cell, dataSource(of:), delegate(of:), FixedDataSource, RecordingDelegate). All 7 suites use them; 140 tests in 7 suites still pass. Lint, both docbuilds and the demo build pass. Reviewed the dependents (4qn.1,.2,.3,.5,.6,.9,.12,.13): none relies on the old per-suite helpers; CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md now point new set-up at TestSupport.swift. Commit f5c7bd7.

title: Simplify CalendarView setup: drop the redundant awakeFromNib and hold observers as cancellables
description:
## Now
setup() is guarded by 'collectionView.superview == nil' because it is called from init(frame:), init(coder:) and awakeFromNib (CalendarView.swift:269-335). init(coder:) always runs first, so the awakeFromNib call (with its MainActor.assumeIsolated) never does anything. Notification observers are stored as nonisolated(unsafe) tokens and removed in deinit (154, 329-341). setup() also mixes block comments (/* Header View */) with configuration that belongs to the layout (section inset and spacing, which CalendarFlowLayout ignores).

## Proposal
Remove the awakeFromNib override and the guard; call setup() from both initialisers. Observe with NotificationCenter.default.publisher(for:) into a Set<AnyCancellable> (or one Task over notifications(named:)), so there is no deinit and no nonisolated(unsafe). Drop the flow-layout settings the custom layout never reads.

## Pattern
Resource ownership (RAII): the subscription lives and dies with the view, with nothing to remember in deinit.
notes: After the CalendarView-4qn.4 file split (pure move) the cited code now lives at: init/awakeFromNib/setup CalendarView.swift:137-203, observers CalendarView.swift:76, deinit CalendarView.swift:205-209.
close_reason: Done in 07e3d09: awakeFromNib override and guard removed, setup() called once per initialiser; observers held in Set<AnyCancellable> (block observers on .main kept for synchronous delivery the today tests rely on), no deinit or nonisolated(unsafe); unused flow-layout insets/spacing dropped. Lint, 142 tests, both docbuilds and the demo build pass.

title: Lay out the weekday labels with a stack view instead of frame maths
description:
## Now
CalendarHeaderView.layoutSubviews (CalendarHeaderView.swift:95-129) computes every frame by hand, including a manual right-to-left walk that starts at the right edge and steps backwards. The month label height subtracts four margins inline. The public updateStyle() shares its name with CalendarView.updateStyle() but does something different and is only meant to be called through setStyle(_:formatters:).

## Proposal
Weekday labels in a horizontal UIStackView with .fillEqually, which mirrors with semanticContentAttribute on its own; the month label and the stack pinned with constraints from the style's margins (updated in setStyle). Make updateStyle private (or rename it applyStyle) as part of rlq.5 if it must stay public. Check the RTL and header tests still pass and compare screenshots in both directions.
close_reason: Weekday labels in a .fillEqually UIStackView that mirrors with the header's semantic content attribute; month label and stack pinned by constraints from the style's margins, updated on restyle. Full test suite (144 tests), both docbuilds, demo build and strict lint pass. Before/after demo screenshots match in LTR and RTL apart from weekday-row anti-aliasing (the stack rounds the column widths to whole pixels). updateStyle() stays public (shipped in 2.1.0); deprecating or renaming it is noted on CalendarView-rlq.5.

title: Move cell-shape geometry onto CellShapeOptions and name the cell's metrics
description:
## Now
CalendarDayCell.layoutSubviews (CalendarDayCell.swift:166-196) uses unnamed numbers (inset 3.0, dot size 0.08 of the height, dot at 2.5 sizes from the bottom, a 'square of' comment) and decides the shape twice: style.cellShape.isRound to square the frame, then a switch for the corner radius. CellShapeOptions.isRound exists only for this.

## Proposal
CellShapeOptions gets internal func backgroundFrame(in:) and cornerRadius(for:), so the cell asks the shape instead of switching on it, and isRound goes. The numbers become named static constants in a private Metrics enum in the cell file (contentInset, dotDiameterRatio, dotBottomOffset).

## Pattern
Tell, don't ask: the enum that knows the shape computes its geometry.
close_reason: CellShapeOptions gains backgroundFrame(in:) and cornerRadius(for:); isRound removed; cell metrics named in a private Metrics enum; geometry test added. Lint, 144 tests, both docbuilds and the demo build pass. Commit ccbaf8a.

title: Make EventsManager an injectable instance instead of a store parameter on every call
description:
## Now
EventsManager is a caseless enum of statics, and every call threads 'store: any CalendarEventStore = EventsManager.store' as a defaulted parameter: load, save, add, and on CalendarView loadEvents (twice), saveEvent and addEvent (EventsManager.swift:133-224) - six copies of the same default. add(event:) and addEvent(...) are Bool wrappers that re-implement save with try?.

## Proposal
public struct EventsManager { let store: any CalendarEventStore ; static let shared = EventsManager(store: EKEventStore()) ; func load/save }. CalendarView gets one stored eventsManager (default .shared) instead of a parameter per method. Keep the current static methods and parameters as deprecated forwarders so 2.x callers still compile; remove them with rlq.5.

## Pattern
Dependency injection through an instance: the dependency is set once, not passed on every call.
notes: From 4qn.11: the chunking statics (maximumQueryLength, queryIntervals) left EventsManager for TimeInterval.eventKitQueryLimit and DateInterval.chunked(maxDuration:), so the enum-to-struct change has nothing of them to carry over.
close_reason: EventsManager is now a struct around one CalendarEventStore (EventsManager.shared, EventsManager(store:)); CalendarView.eventsManager (associated object, .shared default) replaces the per-call store parameter. 2.1 statics and store: overloads kept as deprecated forwarders (removal noted on rlq.5). Lint, 143 tests, both docbuilds and the demo build pass. Commit d51bf11.

title: Split KDCalendarView.updateUIView and the coordinator's repeated callbacks
description:
## Now
updateUIView (CalendarView+SwiftUI.swift:177-226) is 50 lines mixing property sync, a selection-mode change with its bindingIsShown/bindingFollowsView flags, range and event diffing, the display date, and the selection sync with two near-identical branches that both end in correctSelection. In the coordinator, didSelectRange, didSelectDate and didDeselectDate have the same body (guard !isUpdating; parent.selection = calendar.selectedDates), and 'defer until the update ends' is written out twice (correctSelection and didScrollToMonth, each with Task { @MainActor in ... }).

## Proposal
updateUIView calls applyConfiguration(to:), applyContent(to:coordinator:) and syncSelection(of:coordinator:modeChanged:). The coordinator gets selectionChanged(in:) used by the three callbacks, and afterUpdate(_ action:) that runs at once outside an update and defers inside one. Behaviour unchanged; PlatformTests cover it.
notes: Reviewed after CalendarView-4qn.8 (b677848): the modifiers collapsed to one-liners, so updateUIView moved up ~41 lines (now around 136-185). Proposal unaffected.
close_reason: updateUIView split into applyConfiguration/applyContent/syncSelection; coordinator gets selectionChanged(in:) and afterUpdate(_:). Lint, package tests (PlatformTests cover the wrapper), both docbuilds and the example app build pass. Dependent 4qn.16 reviewed and noted.

title: Replace the twelve copy-and-return SwiftUI modifiers with one helper
description:
## Now
CalendarView+SwiftUI.swift has twelve modifiers that each read 'var copy = self; copy.x = value; return copy' (lines 58-162), about 70 lines of boilerplate.

## Proposal
private func with<Value>(_ keyPath: WritableKeyPath<Self, Value>, _ value: Value) -> Self, so each modifier is one line: public func direction(_ direction: ...) -> Self { with(\.direction, direction) }. Documentation comments stay on each modifier.

## Pattern
The functional setter / builder used by SwiftUI's own modifiers.
close_reason: Twelve modifiers now call a private with(_:_:) key-path helper (b677848). Lint, 140 package tests, both docbuilds and the demo build pass.

title: Rename MonthGrid's members so day numbers, dates and grid offsets read differently
description:
## Now
MonthGrid.Month.firstDay is an Int, the grid column of the first day (CalendarView+DataSource.swift:39), while firstDay(ofSection:) returns a Date (line 88), firstDate is a Date and startDay is a Date. daysTotal is a count. isOutOfRange(_:) compares IndexPaths with < and > (line 137-139), which is correct only because sections and items happen to sort like dates. Readers must check types to know what 'firstDay' means.

## Proposal
Month.leadingBlankCells (or firstColumn), Month.dayCount, firstDate kept; firstDayOfMonth(inSection:) for the Date; isOutOfRange compares the cell's date with startDay...endDay. MonthGrid moves to its own file (see the file split bead). The public getCachedSectionInfo keeps its tuple labels until rlq.5 removes it.
notes: After the CalendarView-4qn.4 file split (pure move) the cited code now lives at: MonthGrid now has its own file: Month.firstDay MonthGrid.swift:14, firstDay(ofSection:) MonthGrid.swift:63, isOutOfRange MonthGrid.swift:112-114. getCachedSectionInfo is in the grid extension of CalendarView.swift.
close_reason: Month.firstColumn/dayCount, firstDayOfMonth(inSection:), date-based isOutOfRange; start/endIndexPath removed. getCachedSectionInfo keeps its labels. Lint, 143 tests, both docbuilds and the demo build pass. Commit 6210d24. Reviewed 4qn.16: it cites none of the renamed code.

title: Extract the event index into a pure EventIndex type
description:
## Now
rebuildEventIndex() (CalendarView+DataSource.swift:199-219) is a method on the view that fills the eventsByIndexPath dictionary from events and months, mixing the clamping of open-ended events, DST-safe day stepping and bucketing. It can only be tested through a full CalendarView. Long-press and selection look up eventsByIndexPath[indexPath] ?? [] in several places.

## Proposal
struct EventIndex { init(events:grid:) ; subscript(indexPath) -> [CalendarEvent] (empty by default) ; count(at:) }. Pure and unit-testable in EngineTests next to MonthGrid. The snapshot bead stores one.
notes: After the CalendarView-4qn.4 file split (pure move) the cited code now lives at: rebuildEventIndex() CalendarView.swift:381-401 (the grid extension); the long-press lookup is in CalendarView.swift (handleLongPress), the selection one in CalendarView+Selection.swift (didSelect).
close_reason: EventIndex(events:grid:) extracted into Sources/KDCalendar/EventIndex.swift with subscript, count(at:) and isEmpty; view, data source and selection read it. Pure tests in EngineTests. Lint, 144 tests, both docbuilds and the demo build pass. Pre-existing edge case filed as CalendarView-4qn.19.

title: Handle a change of calendar or time zone in one place
description:
## Now
The view juggles four calendars: style.calendar, style.resolvedCalendar (= CalendarView.calendar), its .fixed copy, and the copies stored in MonthGrid.calendar and Formatters.calendar. A calendar change is detected in two places with two different checks: updateStyle() (CalendarView.swift:432-441) captures months?.calendar, invalidates and moves the selection, while refreshMonths() (CalendarView+DataSource.swift:154-170) compares formatters.calendar to rebuild formatters and months.calendar to move the selection. Readers have to work out which copy each line uses (e.g. rebuildEventIndex uses self.calendar, the grid uses its own).

## Proposal
Compute the effective calendar once per reload (resolved and fixed) and compare it with the one the current snapshot was built with. When it differs: rebuild the formatters, move the selection and rebuild the grid, in that one branch. Everything else reads the snapshot's calendar. Name it for what it is, e.g. layoutCalendar. Pairs with the snapshot bead.
notes: After the CalendarView-4qn.4 file split (pure move) the cited code now lives at: updateStyle() CalendarView.swift:291-300, refreshMonths() calendar handling CalendarView.swift:336-352, moveSelection(from:) in CalendarView+Selection.swift.

title: Assigning dataSource keeps a month grid built without it
description: CalendarView.dataSource has no didSet. Anything that builds the month grid before the data source is assigned (e.g. setting style, which calls updateStyle -> reloadData -> refreshMonths) caches a one-month grid for today. Until the next reloadData or collection view layout refreshes it, indexPathForDate / setDisplayDate / selectDate ignore dates in the data source's range. Seen in UIKit code that sets style before dataSource and then calls setDisplayDate before layout (found writing the test for CalendarView-win.1). KDCalendarView assigns the data source first, so SwiftUI is not affected. Fix: invalidate the grid (invalidateMonths + reloadData) when dataSource is assigned, as UICollectionView does.
close_reason: dataSource didSet invalidates the grid and reloads. Regression test assigningADataSourceReplacesAGridBuiltWithoutIt fails without the fix. Lint, 131 tests and the example build pass. Commit 64adb4b.

title: Range selection drops its last day after a skipped midnight
description:
selectRange (CalendarView.swift) and completeRange (CalendarView+Delegate.swift) walk the range with calendar.date(byAdding: .day, value: 1, to: day) and stop at 'day <= upper', where upper is the start of the last day. In a time zone whose DST change skips midnight (America/Santiago, America/Havana, Asia/Beirut, ...) the step lands on 01:00 on the change day and stays at 01:00 afterwards, so the last day (00:00) fails 'day <= upper' and is left out.

Verified with Foundation in America/Santiago, 6 to 10 Sep 2024 (DST starts Sunday 8 Sep): the loop visits 6, 7, 8 (01:00), 9 (01:00) and never 10 Sep.

Since CalendarView-bl0.1 the stored days come from dateFromIndexPath, so the selection itself stays consistent; only the missing last day remains. Fix: step with calendar.startOfDay(for: next), or walk the grid's index paths. Add a regression test in a Santiago calendar.
close_reason: Fix already in selectableDays(in:) since CalendarView-rlq.1 (steps with startOfDay). Added Santiago regression test covering selectRange and two-tap range completion; verified it fails with the old step. Full suite (131 tests) and swift-format lint pass. Related: CalendarView-6f9.

title: Make EventsManager errors explicit instead of Bool and try?
description:
EventsManager.load swallows the error from requestFullAccess with try? and reports every failure as .authorization (EventsManager.swift:97); add(event:) and CalendarView.addEvent return false for both 'no access' and 'store refused the event', dropping the underlying error. EventsManager.store is a global mutable static, so tests and apps share one store.

Proposal: add throwing variants (e.g. addEvent(...) throws with .authorization or the store's error) and keep the Bool versions as thin wrappers; consider passing the store to CalendarView (a property defaulting to the shared store) rather than a global.
close_reason: Throwing EventsManager.save(_:store:) and CalendarView.saveEvent(_:store:); Bool add variants wrap them; load passes on request errors; store injected per call (EventsManager.store now an immutable shared EKEventStore). Lint, 130 tests, docbuild and example build pass.

title: Give CalendarDayCell a single configuration instead of six observed flags
description:
CalendarDayCell has isToday, isOutOfRange, isAdjacent, isWeekend, isSelected and style, each calling applyStyle() on set, so configuring one cell restyles it six or more times and clearStyles() another six. The day property parses its value back out of the label text (CalendarDayCell.swift:49-58).

Proposal: a DayCellConfiguration value (day number, date, flags, event count, style, accessibility label) applied in one call from cellForItemAt; applyStyle runs once. Keeps the precedence rules in one tested function.
close_reason: CalendarDayCell takes one DayCellConfiguration applied in a single pass from cellForItemAt; precedence lives in DayCellConfiguration.appearance(isSelected:) with its own test. swift-format lint, 129 package tests and the example build pass.

title: Remove implicitly unwrapped views and the Auto Layout flag on frame-laid views
description:
CalendarView.headerView and collectionView are UIView! (CalendarView.swift:103-104) and CalendarHeaderView.monthLabel is UILabel!, although setup() always creates them; the code then mixes force-unwrapping and optional chaining (self.headerView?.frame, self.collectionView.frame). CalendarHeaderView sets translatesAutoresizingMaskIntoConstraints = false on itself and its labels (CalendarHeaderView.swift:53-65) but lays them out with frames, which leaves them ambiguous if the view ever participates in Auto Layout.

Proposal: create the subviews as let properties at declaration (the decoded-view path already rebuilds them), drop the optional chaining, and leave translatesAutoresizingMaskIntoConstraints at its default for frame-laid views.
close_reason: headerView, collectionView, monthLabel and dayLabels are let properties; optional chaining/nil guards removed; translatesAutoresizingMaskIntoConstraints left at default on frame-laid header views. swift-format lint --strict, 127 package tests, and the example app build pass. Commit b4dcc63.

title: Tidy the public API surface ahead of 3.0
description:
The public surface mixes current and legacy API with little to separate them:
- Legacy names kept for 1.x: multipleSelectionEnable, forceLtr, enableDeselection (vs allowsDeselection in SwiftUI), getCachedSectionInfo(_:), cellReuseIdentifier, Style.Default and CellOutOfRangeDisplayOptions (both already deprecated).
- CalendarDayCell, CalendarHeaderView and CalendarFlowLayout are open, but their state (style, day, isToday...) is internal, so subclasses cannot customise anything; CalendarView is public but uses open overrides.
- dateFromIndexPath/indexPathForDate expose the grid's index paths as public API.

Proposal: mark the legacy members deprecated with renamed: targets now, decide which classes are real extension points (make them final or give them public hooks), and remove the rest in 3.0. Record the plan in MigratingFrom1.md.
notes:
Orchestra: worker in Herdr tab w2K:tQ settled with the ticket still 'open'; deferred for review (worktree /Users/michailmichailidis/Projects/CalendarView-worktrees/CalendarView-rlq.5).
worker finished without closing; see Herdr tab w2K:tQ and worktree /Users/michailmichailidis/Projects/CalendarView-worktrees/CalendarView-rlq.5
Triage (orchestra): cause = environment (high confidence). Auto-mode Bash safety check errored on every command; worker never claimed or started. Recommendation: First confirm the auto-mode safety check works again: run `bd show CalendarView-rlq.5` in a fresh auto-mode session. If it fails, run the worker outside auto mode. Before re-queuing, fill in the `<check command>` and `<a quicker subset>` placeholders in the orchestra prompt template (for example `xcodebuild -scheme KDCalendar-Package test` on a simulator only this worktree uses), then run `bd update CalendarView-rlq.5 --status open` so it gets picked up again.
From CalendarView-4qn.10: remove the deprecated EventsManager statics (store, hasFullAccess, load(from:to:store:), save(_:store:), add(event:store:)), the deprecated store: overloads of CalendarView.loadEvents/saveEvent/addEvent, and the DeprecatedForms test in EventKitTests.swift that exercises them.
From CalendarView-4qn.13: CalendarHeaderView.updateStyle() is public (shipped in 2.1.0) but only meant to be called through setStyle(_:formatters:), and it shares its name with the internal CalendarView.updateStyle(). Deprecate it (or rename it applyStyle) here and make it private in 3.0.

title: Centralise date formatters and use one calendar for them
description:
A new DateFormatter is created every time the month settles (displayDateOnHeader, CalendarView+Delegate.swift:194) and every time the header restyles (CalendarHeaderView.updateStyle), and the accessibility formatter is reconfigured for every cell (CalendarView.swift:245). They are configured with style.calendar while the grid uses CalendarView.calendar (style.calendar with the locale filled in), so the two can disagree.

Proposal: build the month-title, weekday and accessibility formatters once per style (e.g. a Formatters struct rebuilt in updateStyle), all from the locale-filled calendar.
close_reason: CalendarView.Formatters (month title, weekday symbols, VoiceOver) built once per style from resolvedCalendar.fixed, rebuilt on style or time zone change and shared with the header. Commit 175927a. Full check passed: swift-format lint --strict, package tests (127), docbuild for both schemes, example build.

title: Replace the negative-scale transforms used for right-to-left
description:
Right-to-left is done by scaling the collection view by -1 and scaling every cell by -1 again (CalendarView.swift:436, CalendarView+DataSource.swift:225), tracked by an _isRtl flag, while the header mirrors separately through semanticContentAttribute. Double transforms complicate hit-testing, layout debugging and snapshot tests.

Proposal: set the collection view's semanticContentAttribute from forceLtr and override flipsHorizontallyInOppositeLayoutDirection in the layout so UIKit mirrors item frames; drop _isRtl and the cell transforms. The ScrollingTests RTL cases cover the behaviour.
close_reason: CalendarFlowLayout mirrors RTL frames (day columns and horizontal month pages); _isRtl and both -1 transforms removed; collection view semanticContentAttribute follows forceLtr. UIKit's flipsHorizontallyInOppositeLayoutDirection did not mirror the hand-built frames (verified on the simulator), so the layout mirrors them itself and answers rect queries from its own frames. Full package tests (127), swift-format lint, example build and docbuild pass. Commit 10c2f6f.

title: Move per-cell content out of cellForItemAt into MonthGrid
description:
collectionView(_:cellForItemAt:) (CalendarView+DataSource.swift:217-270) recomputes the month's first and last index that MonthGrid already knows, calls months.date(at:) three times for the same cell, and does the adjacent-day arithmetic inline, including the section-0 special case.

Proposal: MonthGrid.content(at:) -> enum { day(Date, dayOfMonth), leading(dayOfMonth), trailing(dayOfMonth), empty }, unit-tested in EngineTests. cellForItemAt then becomes a switch that only configures the cell.
close_reason: MonthGrid.content(at:) added with EngineTests; cellForItemAt is a switch. swift-format lint --strict and the package tests (126) pass.

title: Border colours are resolved without the cell's trait collection
description:
CalendarDayCell.applyStyle (CalendarDayCell.swift:174,178) sets layer.borderColor from style colours with .cgColor, which resolves a dynamic UIColor against UITraitCollection.current. applyStyle runs from property observers during cellForItemAt and from the trait-change handler, where the current trait collection is not guaranteed to be the cell's. The defaults are static colours, so only apps passing dynamic border colours are affected.

Confirm: set cellSelectedBorderColor to a dynamic colour, force dark mode on the view only (overrideUserInterfaceStyle), and inspect layer.borderColor. Fix: use colour.resolvedColor(with: traitCollection).cgColor.
close_reason: Border colours resolved with the cell's traitCollection; regression test added. Lint, 124 tests, docbuild and example build pass.

title: onScrollToMonth can fire during a SwiftUI view update
description:
In updateUIView (CalendarView+SwiftUI.swift:174-177), a non-animated displayDate change calls view.setDisplayDate, which calls notifyScrolled and so the coordinator's didScrollToMonth, which runs parent.onScrollToMonth synchronously. The demo assigns @State in that closure (SwiftUIDemoView: .onScrollToMonth { month = $0 }), which SwiftUI flags as 'Modifying state during view update' and can drop or loop.

Confirm by running the SwiftUI demo with the runtime warning breakpoint. Fix: defer the callback (DispatchQueue.main.async or Task { @MainActor in }) while coordinator.isUpdating is true.
notes: Since CalendarView-win.1 (4f7efc6), an animated displayDate change also notifies synchronously when the view has no size yet or the month is already on screen, so the same state-during-update path now happens for animated updates too. Deferring the callback while coordinator.isUpdating covers both.
close_reason: Coordinator defers onScrollToMonth to the main actor while isUpdating (covers animated and non-animated displayDate changes). New test swiftUIDisplayDateChangeReportsTheMonthAfterTheViewUpdate fails without the fix. Full package tests (123), swift-format lint and demo build pass. Commit 101604a.

title: EventKit fetch runs synchronously on the main actor
description:
EventsManager and CalendarEventStore are @MainActor, so EKEventStore.events(matching:) (EventsManager.swift:62) runs on the main thread even though loadEvents() is async. Apple documents events(matching:) as synchronous and potentially slow; for a range of a year or more across several calendars it can hitch scrolling.

Confirm with Instruments on a device with a busy calendar. Fix: perform the fetch off the main actor (the store is thread-safe for reads) and hop back to assign events; keep CalendarEventStore's test double simple.
close_reason: EKEventStore.events(from:to:) is nonisolated async so the chunked EventKit query runs off the main actor; CalendarEventStore.events is async. New test subclasses EKEventStore and checks no query runs on the main thread (fails without the fix). Lint, 123 tests, both docbuilds and the example build pass locally. Not profiled in Instruments on a device. Avoided @concurrent to keep Swift 6.0 (tools-version) compatibility. Commit 37e8bb0.

title: selectRange walks every day of an unbounded range
description:
selectRange(_:) (CalendarView.swift:541) loops day by day from range.lowerBound to range.upperBound, calling the calendar and the delegate's canSelectDate on each, before discarding days outside the grid. completeRange is bounded by the grid, but selectRange takes any ClosedRange from the caller.

Scenario: selectRange(Date.distantPast...Date.distantFuture) or a range of a few decades iterates over a million days on the main thread.

Fix: clamp the range to dateRange (or the displayed months) before the loop. Add a test with a very wide range.
close_reason: Clamp already present: selectableDays(in:) bounds the walk to dateRange (landed with CalendarView-bl0.2). Strengthened the far-off-ends test in cc063a3 to record the days canSelectDate is asked about and to cover a range entirely outside the calendar. swift-format lint --strict and the full package suite (121 tests) pass.

title: Default style snapshots Calendar.current and Locale.current, so time zone changes are not picked up
description:
Style.calendar defaults to Calendar.current and Style.locale to Locale.current (CalendarView+Style.swift:167,171); Style.default is a static let. Both are snapshots, not the autoupdating variants. CalendarView observes significantTimeChangeNotification to keep the today marker honest across time zone changes (CalendarView.swift:333), but the reload computes 'today' with the old time zone.

Scenario: the user travels and the device time zone changes while the app is running. Today's marker and startOfDay-based dates stay in the old zone until the style is replaced.

Confirm on a simulator by changing TZ with the app running. Fix: default to Calendar.autoupdatingCurrent and Locale.autoupdatingCurrent (check that Equatable comparisons in refreshMonths still behave), or refresh the style's calendar when the notification arrives.
close_reason: Default Style.calendar/locale are now Calendar/Locale.autoupdatingCurrent; MonthGrid keeps a fixed calendar copy so a time zone change rebuilds the grid and moves the selection. Regression test theDefaultCalendarFollowsTheDeviceToAnotherTimeZone (fails without the fix). Full tests (122), docbuild, demo build and swift-format lint pass. Commit bd760ff.

title: CalendarFlowLayout overrides frames but keeps the flow layout's content size and culling
description:
CalendarFlowLayout (CalendarFlowLayout.swift) repositions every item into a 7x6 page grid, but collectionViewContentSize and the set of items returned by layoutAttributesForElements(in:) still come from UICollectionViewFlowLayout's own flow of the items. The two agree only while seven items fit exactly in a row (vertical) or six in a column (horizontal). If the flow wraps differently, the content size stops being a whole number of pages and items whose custom frame is on screen but whose flow frame is not are culled, leaving blank cells.

Verified that width/7*7 == width for common iPhone and iPad widths, so this has not been seen, but the collection view's size can be fractional (Auto Layout insets, split view, Dynamic Type headers). Also uses collectionView.frame (not bounds) and fatalError() in @unknown default where the rest of the code falls back to horizontal.

Confirm: lay out at fractional sizes (e.g. 361.33 x 300.67) in both directions and compare collectionViewContentSize to sections x page size and the visible cells to 42. Fix: subclass UICollectionViewLayout directly (or use a compositional layout) and compute content size and attributes from the page geometry.
close_reason: CalendarFlowLayout now computes content size, cells in a rect and item attributes from the 7x6 page grid; invalidates on bounds size change; @unknown default falls back to horizontal; bounds instead of frame. Regression test fractionalSizesKeepWholePagesAndEveryCell (258 1/3 x 300, both directions) fails on the old layout and passes now. Full xcodebuild test (112 passed), swift-format lint, example build and docbuild pass. Commit fa9acec.

title: A drag that ends without deceleration does not report the month
description:
CalendarView+Delegate.swift handles scrollViewDidEndDecelerating and scrollViewDidEndScrollingAnimation, but not scrollViewDidEndDragging(_:willDecelerate: false). With paging enabled UIKit nearly always decelerates to snap, but a drag released exactly on a page boundary, or a paging interaction interrupted programmatically, ends without either callback. The header and didScrollToMonth then stay on the old month.

Confirm: deliver scrollViewDidEndDragging(willDecelerate: false) at another page's offset in ScrollingTests. Fix: call updateAndNotifyScrolling() there when willDecelerate is false.
close_reason: scrollViewDidEndDragging(willDecelerate: false) now calls updateAndNotifyScrolling(); new ScrollingTests case covers both branches. Full package tests (111) and swift-format lint --strict pass. Commit dd30231.

title: Review: structure and readability
description: Refactors from the September 2026 review that would make the code easier to read, test and change. None change behaviour on their own unless noted.

title: An event ending at the grid's first midnight marks day one
description: EventIndex(events:grid:) (Sources/KDCalendar/EventIndex.swift) keeps an event when eventEnd >= gridStart and its repeat-while loop always marks the first day. So an event from 31 Dec 10:00 to 1 Jan 00:00, with the grid starting on 1 January, marks 1 January, while an event ending at midnight anywhere else in the grid stays on its own day (CalendarViewTests.eventsMarkEveryDayTheyCover, 'an event ending at midnight stays on its day'). Zero-length events at a midnight should still mark their day. Fix: skip the first day when last <= day and the event started before it; add a case to the EventIndex tests in EngineTests. Pre-existing; found while extracting EventIndex in CalendarView-4qn.6, which kept the behaviour unchanged.
notes:
Blocked on CalendarView-4qn.6 merging: EventIndex.swift and the EventIndex tests in EngineTests exist only on wt/CalendarView-4qn.6 (b998480), which is not yet on main or this branch (based on a43b652). Fixing the loop at its old place (CalendarView.swift:368-380) would conflict with 4qn.6 moving that code, and the worker prompt forbids merging other branches. Retry once 4qn.6 is merged. No code changed.
Triage (orchestra): cause = problem (high confidence). Fix targets EventIndex.swift, which exists only on unmerged CalendarView-4qn.6 branch. Recommendation: Merge wt/CalendarView-4qn.6 (b998480) into main. Then run `bd dep add CalendarView-4qn.19 CalendarView-4qn.6`, undefer 4qn.19 and re-dispatch it on a fresh branch from main; the pending "cherry-pick" message in the terminal was never acted on. While you're at it, fill in the `<check command>` placeholders in the worker prompt template.

title: Make the long-press callback's events non-optional like the selection callback's
description:
## Now
calendar(_:didLongPressDate:withEvents:) takes [CalendarEvent]? where nil means none (CalendarView.swift:78, 359), while didSelectDate takes a non-optional array where empty means none. The SwiftUI coordinator converts with 'events ?? []'. Two conventions for the same fact.

## Proposal
Use a non-optional array in 3.0; add the new requirement with a default that calls the old one for a release so conformers keep compiling. Decide together with CalendarView-rlq.5.
notes: Deferred with CalendarView-rlq.5: a public API change for 3.0 that needs the maintainer's decision, not an unattended worker. Undefer to schedule it.

title: Consistency pass: explicit self, legacy comments and small inaccuracies
description:
## Now
Mixed idioms from different eras: 163 explicit self. in Sources where most code omits it; block comments like /* Layout */ and 'MARK: - public' in front of internal members (CalendarView.swift:169); UIColor.clear next to .clear; return in single-expression bodies; numberOfItemsInSection's comment says 'rows:7 x cols:6' when it is seven columns by six rows (CalendarView+DataSource.swift:250); the MIT header on most files but none on SelectionState.swift and CalendarView+Formatters.swift.

## Proposal
One mechanical commit, no behaviour change: drop redundant self., fix the MARKs and the comment, align the file headers, prefer type-inferred members. Run after the larger refactors so it does not cause conflicts with them.
notes:
Reviewed after CalendarView-4qn.9: updateUIView in CalendarView+SwiftUI.swift is now split into applyConfiguration/applyContent/syncSelection, and the moved bodies keep their explicit self. (left for this pass). Proposal unaffected.
CalendarView-4qn.14 (07e3d09) already removed the /* Header View */, /* Layout */ and /* Collection View */ block comments from CalendarView.setup(); the explicit self. there is left for this pass.
Reviewed after CalendarView-4qn.6: the explicit self. in handleLongPress (self.eventIndex) is left for this pass; new EventIndex.swift has no MIT header, like MonthGrid.swift and SelectionState.swift. Proposal unaffected.
Reviewed after CalendarView-4qn.10: EventsManager.swift's CalendarView extension (loadEvents/saveEvent/addEvent and their private using: helpers) keeps the explicit self. it had (self.dateRange, self.events, self.calendar); left for this pass. Proposal unaffected.

title: Express the four-year EventKit chunking as DateInterval.chunked(maxLength:)
description:
## Now
EventsManager.queryIntervals(from:to:) returns [(start: Date, end: Date)] tuples (EventsManager.swift:118-128), and the de-duplication struct Occurrence is declared inside events(from:to:). The intent - split an interval into pieces EventKit accepts - is hidden in a static on the manager.

## Proposal
extension DateInterval { func chunked(maxDuration: TimeInterval) -> [DateInterval] }, tested on its own; events(from:to:) reads 'for chunk in DateInterval(start:end:).chunked(maxDuration: .eventKitQueryLimit)'. Occurrence becomes a file-private type with a one-line comment on why recurring events need the start date.
close_reason: Chunking is DateInterval.chunked(maxDuration:) with TimeInterval.eventKitQueryLimit; Occurrence is file-private. Named maxDuration (per the description and DateInterval.duration) rather than maxLength from the title. A backwards interval returns [] without querying. Lint, 142 tests, both docbuilds and the demo build pass. Dependent 4qn.10 reviewed: no conflict.

title: Event index skips the day after a skipped midnight
description: rebuildEventIndex (CalendarView+DataSource.swift) steps day = calendar.date(byAdding: .day, value: 1, to: day) without returning to startOfDay, and loops while day < last (the event's end). In a zone whose DST change skips midnight (America/Santiago, 8 Sep 2024) the walk sits at 01:00 from the change day on, so an event ending between 00:00 and 01:00 on a later day (e.g. 6 Sep 10:00 to 10 Sep 00:30) is not indexed on that last day, although it would be without DST. Same class as CalendarView-p0p. Fix: day = calendar.startOfDay(for: next), as selectableDays(in:) does; add a Santiago test.
close_reason: rebuildEventIndex now steps to startOfDay(for:) after each day; Santiago regression test added (fails before, passes after). Full package suite 134/134 and swift-format lint pass. Commit 97ff0a3.

title: Reapply cell borders on a contrast trait change
description: CalendarDayCell registers for UITraitUserInterfaceStyle changes only, to reapply its CGColor borders. Since win.8 the border colours are resolved against the cell's full traitCollection, so a dynamic border colour that varies with accessibilityContrast (Increase Contrast) keeps its old value until another flag changes. Consider also registering UITraitAccessibilityContrast (and any other trait the colours may depend on).
close_reason: CalendarDayCell registers for UITraitCollection.systemTraitsAffectingColorAppearance (style, contrast, level, ...) instead of userInterfaceStyle only. New test cellBordersFollowAContrastChange fails without the fix. Full package tests (134), example build and swift-format lint pass. Commit 8e818ba.

title: Fix DocC link to internal CalendarDayCell.configuration
description: docbuild of KDCalendar warns: 'configuration' doesn't exist at '/KDCalendar/CalendarDayCell' (CalendarDayCell.swift:99). The public class doc links ``configuration``, an internal property added in rlq.7, so DocC cannot resolve it. Use plain code voice or describe it without a symbol link.
close_reason: Doc comment no longer links the internal configuration property; docbuild of KDCalendar and KDCalendarEventKit is warning-free and all 133 tests pass.

title: Fill in CLAUDE.md and fix stale release notes in the README
description:
CLAUDE.md still has the bd init template placeholders for Build & Test, Architecture Overview and Conventions. The README says '2.0.0 is the final CocoaPods release' while the podspec is at 2.0.1 and the changelog has unreleased fixes. Source headers are inconsistent (CalendarView+Style.swift has an Xcode template header, the rest the MIT notice).

Proposal: document the xcodebuild test and docbuild commands, the demo launch arguments (-tab N, -sampleEvents), the module layout (KDCalendar, KDCalendarEventKit, MonthGrid as the pure date engine) and swift-format lint --strict; update the CocoaPods note to the actual final version; align the headers.
close_reason: CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md filled in (build/test/docbuild/lint, demo launch args, module layout, conventions); README and migration guide name 2.0.1 as final CocoaPods release; Style and SwiftUI headers use the MIT notice. Lint, package tests, both docbuilds and the example build pass. Commit fbcd1c5.

title: Make CalendarEvent Equatable and Hashable
description:
KDCalendarView.Coordinator compares event arrays field by field in sameEvents(as:) (CalendarView+SwiftUI.swift:204) because CalendarEvent has no Equatable conformance. Apps diffing their own events hit the same gap.

Proposal: conform CalendarEvent to Equatable and Hashable (synthesised), replace sameEvents with ==, and note it in the changelog.
close_reason: CalendarEvent conforms to Hashable (synthesised); sameEvents replaced with ==; changelog entry and test added. swift-format lint and 132 package tests pass.

title: Adjacent days are hidden before the first month but shown after the last
description:
With showAdjacentDays on, cellForItemAt (CalendarView+DataSource.swift:253-264) hides leading cells in section 0 (there is no previous month in the grid to count from) but shows trailing cells in the last section, numbering them into a month that is not in the grid. The two ends of the calendar look different.

Decide the intended behaviour: compute the leading days from the calendar (days in the previous month) so both ends show, or hide both. Low impact, cosmetic.
close_reason: Decided to show both ends: leading days in the first month are now computed from the calendar (MonthGrid.content), matching the trailing days after the last month. Tests updated; swift-format lint, 131 package tests and the example build pass. Commit 42d6e86.
